we propose a semantic bottlenecks GAN for unconditional synthesis of scenes and demonstrate that the end to end training improves the segmentation-to- image synthesis subnetwork.

(1) we introduce a new semantic bottleneck GAN framework for unconditional image synthesis, (2) we demonstrate its effectiveness on two challenging datasets and (3) we show that the end-to end training of the semantic bottleneck model significantly improves the performance of the segmentation-to-image sub-network.

(i) the proposed method is able to learn a semantic bottleneck that can be used to synthesize a wide variety of complex scenes, including indoor scenes, street scenes, and outdoor scenes, and (ii) the proposed method can be trained end-to-end and achieves state-of-the-art results on unsupervised image generation.

the proposed semantic bottleneck GAN can serve as a powerful tool for unconditional image synthesis in a wide variety of domains.
